classes.objetivo: Reconocer cómo un verbo o un adjetivo se convierte en sustantivo (nominalización) para compactar información en un texto académico.

vocabulario.es: nominalización: convertir una acción o cualidad en sustantivo

ensenanza.en: Nominalisation turns actions into nouns, so cities grew rapidly becomes the rapid growth of cities, a compact noun phrase.
ensenanza.es: La nominalización convierte acciones en sustantivos, así que «las ciudades crecieron rápidamente» pasa a «el rápido crecimiento de las ciudades», un grupo nominal compacto.
ensenanza.nota: El verbo grow pasa a growth, el adverbio rapidly pasa a adjetivo rapid y el sujeto original va detrás de of.

ensenanza.en: Dense prose often hides its actors: the adoption of the new method does not say who adopted it or why.
ensenanza.es: La prosa densa suele ocultar a sus protagonistas: «la adopción del nuevo método» no dice quién lo adoptó ni por qué.
ensenanza.nota: Al nominalizar, el verbo adopt se convierte en una cosa y desaparece el sujeto que actuaba.

ensenanza.en: When a sentence seems impenetrable, unpack it: restore the verbs behind the nouns, and then say who did what to whom.
ensenanza.es: Cuando una frase parece impenetrable, desmenúzala: devuelve los verbos que hay detrás de los sustantivos y di quién hizo qué a quién.
ensenanza.nota: Desnominalizar es el camino inverso: del sustantivo abstracto al verbo y a su sujeto.

ensenanza.en: Heightened awareness of the risk led to a significant reduction in accidents, and that nominalisation hides who became aware.
ensenanza.es: Una mayor sensibilización ante el riesgo llevó a una reducción considerable de los accidentes, y esa nominalización oculta quién se volvió consciente.
ensenanza.nota: Aware pasa a awareness y reduce pasa a reduction: dos historias quedan comprimidas en una sola oración.

ensenanza.en: The efficiency of the service improved last year, where plainer writing would say that the service became more efficient.
ensenanza.es: La eficiencia del servicio mejoró el año pasado, donde una redacción más sencilla diría que el servicio se volvió más eficiente.
ensenanza.nota: El adjetivo efficient pasa a efficiency (-ent a -ency); el grupo nominal entero es ahora el sujeto de improved.

ensenanza.en: A technical report may lend itself to nominalisation, but piling up nouns comes at the expense of clarity for any ordinary reader.
ensenanza.es: Un informe técnico puede prestarse a la nominalización, pero acumular sustantivos se hace a costa de la claridad para cualquier lector común.
ensenanza.nota: Lend itself to significa «ser apropiado para»; at the expense of introduce lo que se sacrifica.

explicacion.texto: Los textos académicos prefieren sustantivos a verbos. En vez de «Cities grew rapidly» escriben «the rapid growth of cities»: el verbo (grow, adopt, reduce) o el adjetivo (aware, efficient) pasa a ser sustantivo, el adverbio se vuelve adjetivo y el sujeto original va detrás de of. Así una oración entera cabe en un grupo nominal que sirve de sujeto de otra. Es eficaz, pero oculta quién hace qué: al leer, busca el sustantivo, recupera el verbo y pregúntate quién actuaba. Si acumulas demasiados, pierdes claridad.

patron.texto: Oración verbal → bloque nominal + verbo nuevo:

formula.nota: verbo grow → sustantivo growth; el adverbio pasa a adjetivo
el sujeto original va después de of
el bloque nominal ya es sujeto de una frase nueva

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The grow of cities is rapid.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The growth of cities is rapid.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Grow es el verbo; el sustantivo es growth. No se puede usar el verbo como sustantivo.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The growth rapid of the company surprised us.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The rapid growth of the company surprised us.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En inglés el adjetivo va antes del sustantivo; en español «crecimiento rápido» lo pone detrás.

situacion.contexto: Ana y Leo repasan un artículo de economía para un examen y Leo se atasca con una frase.

dialogo.texto: Ana, I cannot follow this sentence: the council's adoption of the scheme produced a significant reduction in delays.
dialogo.traduccion: Ana, no entiendo esta frase: la adopción del plan por parte del municipio produjo una reducción considerable de los retrasos.

dialogo.texto: It looks like dense prose, but it packs two stories into one. The council adopted the scheme, and delays fell a lot.
dialogo.traduccion: Parece prosa densa, pero empaqueta dos historias en una. El municipio adoptó el plan y los retrasos bajaron mucho.

dialogo.texto: So adoption comes from adopt, and reduction comes from reduce. But who reduced the delays?
dialogo.traduccion: Entonces adoption viene de adopt y reduction de reduce. Pero, ¿quién redujo los retrasos?

dialogo.texto: Exactly. The noun phrase does not say, and that is what you should ask when you unpack a sentence like this.
dialogo.traduccion: Exacto. El grupo nominal no lo dice, y eso es lo que debes preguntarte cuando desmenuzas una frase así.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué detalle deja sin aclarar la frase nominalizada del artículo?

opciones.es: Quién consiguió que los retrasos bajaran.
Cuántos retrasos hubo antes del plan.
Cuándo adoptó el ayuntamiento el plan.

item.feedback: Leo pregunta «who reduced the delays?» y Ana responde que el grupo nominal no lo dice: la nominalización oculta al agente.

guiada.consigna: Elige la versión nominalizada de la oración del informe municipal.
guiada.texto: Since the council adopted the scheme last January, accidents on the ring road have fallen significantly, which has surprised even the engineers.
opciones: The council's adoption of the scheme has led to a significant reduction in accidents on the ring road.
The adoption of the scheme by the council has led to the significant reduce of ring road accidents.
The council's adopting of the scheme has significantly reduction in accidents on the ring road.
guiada.feedback: Adoption sustituye a adopted y reduction a fallen; el adverbio significantly pasa a adjetivo significant delante del sustantivo.
guiada.pista: Busca el sustantivo de adopt y el de reduce; el adverbio pasa a adjetivo.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Su cuidadosa evaluación de las pruebas convenció incluso a los escépticos.»
guiada.texto: The committee studied the proposal for months. Its careful ___ of the evidence convinced even the critics.
guiada.feedback: Assessment es el sustantivo de assess; aquí funciona como núcleo de un grupo nominal con of.
guiada.pista: Es el sustantivo de assess y termina en -ment.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «El rápido crecimiento de la ciudad presionó a las escuelas locales.»
guiada.respuesta: The rapid growth of the city put pressure on local schools
guiada.feedback: El grupo nominal The rapid growth of the city es el sujeto y put pressure on es la parte verbal.
guiada.pista: Empieza por el grupo nominal que hace de sujeto.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada grupo nominal con la idea verbal que esconde.
pares: the assessment of risk by trained experts
the efficiency of the new system
El nuevo sistema funciona con eficiencia
Los vecinos son ahora más conscientes
a significant reduction in waiting times
Los tiempos de espera se redujeron mucho
the rapid growth of the online market
El mercado en línea creció deprisa
practica.feedback: Cada grupo nominal guarda un verbo o adjetivo: assess, efficient, aware, reduce y grow.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué critica la investigadora de la expresión «the fall in confidence».
practica.audio: In her talk, the researcher describes the sudden fall in customer confidence after the announcement. That single noun phrase, she says, hides who lost confidence and why, which is exactly what makes dense prose so hard to question.
opciones: It condenses the event but leaves out who lost confidence and why.
It exaggerates the event by choosing a stronger word than the facts allow.
It makes a serious event sound milder than the figures suggest.
practica.feedback: La investigadora critica que el grupo nominal condensa el hecho y oculta quién perdió la confianza y por qué.

practica.consigna: Completa: «Se menciona la adopción de una política, como si nadie la hubiera elegido.»
practica.texto: The report never names the people in charge. It simply mentions the ___ of a new policy, as if nobody had chosen it.
practica.feedback: Adoption nominaliza el verbo adopt y deja a los responsables sin nombre, como sugiere el resto de la frase.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué sugiere la autora sobre el estilo de este informe?
evaluacion.texto: The committee's conclusion rested on the rapid adoption of the new timetable and a marked reduction in complaints. Nowhere does the report say who chose the timetable, who complained, or how the complaints were counted. The paragraph reads easily, yet its dense prose leaves the reader with figures and no people to question about them.
opciones: That its easy style makes it hard to see who acted and how the figures were obtained.
That the style is so plain and repetitive that the figures cannot be trusted by careful readers.
That the committee left the figures out on purpose to protect itself.
That the complaints fell only because nobody was counting them any more.
evaluacion.feedback: La autora señala que el texto fluye pero no dice quién eligió ni cómo se contó: la prosa densa deja cifras sin personas responsables.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige la actitud de la conferenciante ante el titular.
evaluacion.audio: A lecturer is explaining why she doubts a headline. The headline said: rapid adoption of the app triggers a significant reduction in waste. She points out that the sentence is tidy and convincing, but that it conceals everything a careful reader needs to know. Who adopted the app, and how quickly? Waste of what, and measured by whom? She does not say the claim is false. Her point is that nominalisation lets a writer present a hopeful result as if it were simply a fact, so a reader must unpack the noun phrases before trusting the headline.
opciones: Cautious: she wants the claims unpacked before she accepts them.
Dismissive: she regards the headline as false and wants it dropped.
Curious: she wants to test the app herself and measure its effect on waste.
evaluacion.feedback: Ella no afirma que el titular sea falso, pero pide desmenuzar los grupos nominales antes de creerlo: postura cauta, no de rechazo ni de aplauso.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Los artículos técnicos suelen prestarse a ellas.»
evaluacion.texto: Heavy noun phrases are not wrong in themselves. Technical papers often ___ themselves to them, but a leaflet for the public should stay closer to verbs.
evaluacion.feedback: La colocación es lend itself to, «prestarse a»; con un sujeto plural (papers) el verbo queda en forma base: lend themselves to.

evaluacion.consigna: Fusiona las dos ideas en una sola frase nominalizada, con un verbo de resultado.
evaluacion.texto: Ideas: el servicio se volvió más eficiente (efficient) y por eso los clientes se quejaron menos (complain). Escribe una sola frase que use efficiency y reduction.
evaluacion.respuesta: The improved efficiency of the service led to a significant reduction in complaints from customers.
aceptadas: A greater efficiency of the service resulted in a reduction in the number of complaints.
The efficiency of the service brought about a reduction in complaints, which pleased customers.
evaluacion.feedback: Efficient pasa a efficiency y complain a complaints, y el verbo de resultado (led to) une las dos ideas.

evidencias: reduction in the number of complaints

repaso.consigna: ¿Cuál es la postura del autor ante la nominalización?
repaso.texto: Critics of formal style complain that nominalisation makes writing cold and stiff. I disagree, up to a point. A noun phrase such as the assessment of risk lets a writer name an idea once and then build on it. What I do object to is the crowd of abstract nouns: five of them in a single sentence is not skill, only extra work for the reader.
opciones: Useful when used sparingly, but a nuisance when abstract nouns crowd together.
Acceptable only in reports, and unsuitable for any other kind of text.
Wrongly attacked by critics, who should admire it as a sign of skill.
Cold and stiff in every case, although readers eventually get used to it.
repaso.feedback: El autor defiende el recurso («lets a writer name an idea once») pero rechaza el amontonamiento de cinco sustantivos abstractos.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Una reducción significativa de las quejas siguió al nuevo procedimiento.»
repaso.respuesta: A significant reduction in complaints followed the new method
repaso.feedback: El grupo nominal A significant reduction in complaints es el sujeto de followed.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «El resumen es muy breve, pero a costa de la claridad.»
repaso.texto: The summary is very short, but it has been made so at the ___ of clarity, since none of the people involved are named.
repaso.feedback: At the expense of es la fórmula para lo que se sacrifica; at the cost of y at the price of son variantes posibles.

classes.objetivo: Usar adjetivos evaluativos académicos (robust, flawed, compelling, tentative) para valorar un estudio con su razón, y reconocer la pasiva impersonal.

vocabulario.es: sólido, resistente (un resultado que se mantiene)
no alcanzar, quedarse corto respecto a

ensenanza.en: The results are robust: the sample was large, the method was clear, and the finding survived a second attempt.
ensenanza.es: Los resultados son sólidos: la muestra era grande, el método era claro y el hallazgo resistió un segundo intento.
ensenanza.nota: Robust valora bien un resultado que se mantiene en distintas pruebas; la razón va tras los dos puntos.

ensenanza.en: A flawed design can cast doubt on every result that follows from it, however impressive the figures may look.
ensenanza.es: Un diseño con fallos puede sembrar dudas sobre todos los resultados que se derivan de él, por impresionantes que parezcan las cifras.
ensenanza.nota: Cast doubt on es la colocación para debilitar la confianza en algo; however + adjetivo concede el atractivo de las cifras.

ensenanza.en: The evidence is compelling, since three independent teams found the same effect, and their combined data lend weight to the claim.
ensenanza.es: La evidencia es convincente, ya que tres equipos independientes hallaron el mismo efecto, y sus datos combinados dan peso a la afirmación.
ensenanza.nota: Lend weight to significa «respaldar»; data se usa aquí como plural, por eso lend y no lends.

ensenanza.en: It is widely believed that coffee sharpens memory, but the authors stay tentative about one small study.
ensenanza.es: Se cree ampliamente que el café agudiza la memoria, pero los autores se muestran prudentes ante un solo estudio pequeño.
ensenanza.nota: Repaso de la pasiva impersonal (it is believed that…) junto a tentative, que marca la cautela de los autores.

ensenanza.en: Even a thorough study can leave the proof far from conclusive if its methods fall short of accepted standards.
ensenanza.es: Incluso un estudio minucioso puede dejar la prueba lejos de ser concluyente si sus métodos no alcanzan los estándares aceptados.
ensenanza.nota: Thorough elogia el cuidado; conclusive dice que la cuestión queda cerrada; fall short of = no llegar al nivel exigido.

ensenanza.en: Questionable wording may call into question an otherwise methodologically sound survey, because respondents can read the items differently.
ensenanza.es: Una redacción dudosa puede poner en entredicho una encuesta por lo demás metodológicamente correcta, porque los encuestados pueden leer las preguntas de otro modo.
ensenanza.nota: Questionable es un adjetivo de cautela; call into question = poner en entredicho; otherwise = por lo demás.

explicacion.titulo: Valorar un estudio con el adjetivo preciso
explicacion.texto: Para juzgar un estudio, el inglés académico usa adjetivos que dicen cuánta confianza merece. Robust y compelling valoran bien; flawed y questionable señalan debilidades; thorough elogia el cuidado del trabajo; tentative indica la cautela del autor y conclusive dice que la cuestión queda cerrada. Acompaña siempre el adjetivo con una razón (because, since o dos puntos) y, si quieres matizar, usa fórmulas como cast doubt on, lend weight to o fall short of. Un buen juicio es justo: distingue la calidad del método de la fuerza de la conclusión.

patron.texto: Lo que valoras + be + adjetivo + razón:

formula.nota: lo que valoras: results, evidence, study, method…
razón con because, since o dos puntos

erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Los adjetivos ingleses no concuerdan en plural: robust sirve para uno o para varios.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The study is flaw because the sample was too small.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The study is flawed because the sample was too small.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Flaw es el sustantivo (un fallo); para describir el estudio se necesita el adjetivo flawed.

situacion.contexto: Mia y Tom preparan una exposición sobre un estudio de café y memoria y discuten cómo valorarlo.

dialogo.texto: The results are robust, I think. Three teams found the same thing, and their data lend weight to the claim.
dialogo.traduccion: Creo que los resultados son sólidos. Tres equipos encontraron lo mismo y sus datos respaldan la afirmación.

dialogo.texto: Maybe, but the sample was tiny, only twelve students. That could cast doubt on the whole design.
dialogo.traduccion: Quizá, pero la muestra era diminuta, solo doce estudiantes. Eso podría sembrar dudas sobre todo el diseño.

dialogo.texto: The authors themselves say their results are tentative. They do not call the proof conclusive.
dialogo.traduccion: Los propios autores dicen que sus resultados son provisionales. No llaman concluyente a la prueba.

dialogo.texto: Fair enough. So the evidence is interesting, but not compelling, and we should say exactly that.
dialogo.traduccion: Justo. Entonces la evidencia es interesante, pero no convincente, y deberíamos decir exactamente eso.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿por qué cree Tom que el diseño del estudio puede ser dudoso?

opciones.es: Porque la muestra era de solo doce estudiantes.
Porque los autores reconocen que sus resultados son provisionales.
Porque el estudio no tuvo un grupo de comparación.

item.feedback: Tom señala que «the sample was tiny, only twelve students» y que eso podría sembrar dudas sobre el diseño; los autores, además, son prudentes.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Por eso, el diseño del estudio tiene graves fallos.»
guiada.texto: Only twelve students took part, and all of them were chosen by the researcher's friends. For that reason, the design of the study is seriously ___.
guiada.feedback: Flawed describe un diseño con fallos; la razón (muestra pequeña y elegida por amigos) está en la frase anterior.
guiada.pista: Adjetivo que señala un fallo de diseño y termina en -ed.

guiada.consigna: Elige la valoración que combina el resultado y la actitud de los autores.
guiada.texto: A survey of five thousand adults in six countries found the same pattern each time. The authors, however, write only that it may indicate a link, and they call for further trials before drawing any firm conclusion.
opciones: The findings look robust, while the authors stay tentative.
The findings look flawed, since the authors call for further trials.
The findings look robust, so the authors sound conclusive.
guiada.feedback: El mismo patrón en seis países sugiere resultados sólidos, pero los autores escriben solo «may» y piden más ensayos: son prudentes.
guiada.pista: Un patrón repetido suena sólido; «may» y «further trials» suenan prudentes.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Una muestra tan pequeña siembra dudas sobre todo el estudio.»
guiada.respuesta: Such a small sample casts doubt on the whole study
guiada.feedback: Such a + adjetivo + sustantivo pone el énfasis en el tamaño; casts doubt on sigue a un sujeto singular.
guiada.pista: Such a va antes del adjetivo y del sustantivo.

practica.consigna: Elige el adjetivo que evalúa con precisión cada estudio.
frases: Only ten people took part and the sample was biased, so the design is ___.
The same effect survived every repetition of the test and in every country, so the result is ___.
Three independent teams reached the same view and a careful reader would struggle to disagree, so the case is ___.
The authors call it a first look and ask for more trials, so their conclusion is ___.
practica.feedback: Cada razón apunta a un adjetivo: muestra sesgada, flawed; efecto que resiste cada repetición, robust; argumento al que cuesta oponerse, compelling; primer vistazo, tentative.
practica.texto: Four studies reached the college reading group this week. Evaluate each one with the adjective that fits its evidence best: robust, flawed, compelling or tentative.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué opina la hablante del estudio.
practica.audio: I read the whole paper this morning. The method is thorough, since every step is checked and explained. But the survey questions are questionable, so I would not trust the headline result just yet. I would call the conclusions tentative at best.
opciones: The method impressed her, but the wording of the survey makes her hesitate.
The method impressed her, but the survey wording leads her to reject the paper completely.
The survey wording worried her, but the method made her fully trust the result anyway.
practica.feedback: Elogia el método (thorough), pero duda de las preguntas (questionable) y por eso aplaza su confianza: no rechaza el estudio ni lo acepta sin reservas.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué valoración del experimento es la más precisa?
practica.texto: The team ran the experiment once, with thirty volunteers, and reported a small improvement. They write that the data are consistent with a benefit, but that a larger trial is needed before any firm conclusion can be drawn.
opciones: Tentative: a small first trial that hints at a possible benefit.
Flawed: a single trial with volunteers can never show anything.
Conclusive: a small result that already settles the question.
practica.feedback: El equipo realizó el experimento una sola vez, con treinta voluntarios, y pide un ensayo mayor: es un resultado provisional, no concluyente.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué da a entender la evaluadora sobre la afirmación principal del estudio?
evaluacion.texto: Reviewer's report: The authors have plainly worked hard. Their survey is thorough, and their statistics are handled with care. Yet the headline claim, that green tea improves concentration, rests on a single classroom in one school, with no comparison group. One is left wondering whether the tea, the teacher or the time of day made the difference.
opciones: That careful work does not justify so firm a claim from such limited evidence.
That the statistics are weak and should be repeated by another independent team of researchers.
That the tea obviously has no effect, since the teacher caused the result.
That a comparison group would prove the authors' claim completely.
evaluacion.feedback: La evaluadora elogia el trabajo, pero señala que una sola aula sin grupo de comparación no basta para una afirmación tan firme.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué quiere enseñar la profesora sobre cómo valorar un estudio pequeño.
evaluacion.audio: When you evaluate a study, do not reach for the strongest word. Calling a study flawed because its sample is small is fair only if the authors claim more than that sample allows. A small study that says tentative things can be perfectly honest. Suppose two teams each test forty people. One team writes that the medicine always works; the other writes that the result is encouraging and deserves a larger trial. Their data may be the same, and yet only the first team has gone too far. The real fault is a claim that is bigger than its evidence.
opciones: That a judgement is fair only when the claim is no bigger than the evidence.
That a small sample is an acceptable reason to call any study flawed.
That honest authors should avoid tentative language to sound more convincing.
That a study should be evaluated by the size of its sample and nothing else.
evaluacion.feedback: La profesora dice que un estudio pequeño puede ser honesto si sus afirmaciones son prudentes; el fallo está en la distancia entre evidencia y afirmación.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «El segundo informe no alcanzó el nivel exigido.»
evaluacion.texto: The committee read all three reports with care. The second, however, fell ___ of the standard required, because it gave no details of how the participants were chosen.
evaluacion.feedback: Fall short of es la colocación para «no alcanzar» un nivel o estándar.

evaluacion.consigna: Valora el estudio en dos frases: resultado, razón y actitud de los autores.
evaluacion.texto: Datos: 3000 participantes de cinco países; el mismo resultado en cada réplica del experimento; método revisado paso a paso. Los autores escriben que sus conclusiones son provisionales y piden más ensayos.
evaluacion.respuesta: The results are robust and the method is thorough, since three thousand people in five countries showed the same pattern. Even so, the authors remain tentative and call for more trials before any firm conclusion is drawn.
aceptadas: The findings are robust, because people in five countries produced the same result every time. The authors are tentative, however, and ask for further trials before any firm conclusion is drawn.
The evidence is compelling, since 3000 people in five countries gave the same result. Nevertheless, the authors remain cautious and call for more trials.
evaluacion.feedback: Un buen comentario combina un adjetivo preciso, la razón con datos del estudio y la cautela de los autores.

repaso.consigna: ¿Con qué propósito escribe el autor este párrafo?
repaso.texto: It is widely believed that eating late at night ruins sleep, and advice columns repeat it every winter. Yet a review that pooled thirty trials found no clear effect. The reviewers do not say that late meals are good for you; they say the evidence is simply not there. A claim can be popular, old and comforting without ever becoming well supported.
opciones: To show that a popular idea is not the same as a proven one.
To warn readers that late meals are dangerous for their sleep and their general health.
To argue that thirty trials are too few to decide anything.
To defend late meals against unfair reviews of the evidence.
repaso.feedback: El autor no dice que cenar tarde sea bueno ni malo: señala que una idea puede ser popular y reconfortante sin estar respaldada por pruebas.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Los datos no son concluyentes, pero el estudio es minucioso.»
repaso.respuesta: The data are not conclusive, yet the study is thorough
repaso.feedback: Yet introduce el contraste: lo minucioso del estudio no basta para que los datos sean concluyentes.
aceptadas: The study is thorough, yet the data are not conclusive

repaso.consigna: Relaciona cada fórmula evaluativa con su sentido.
repaso.feedback: Las cuatro fórmulas sirven para valorar: respaldar, poner en entredicho, no alcanzar y sembrar dudas.

classes.objetivo: Leer un abstract y extraer objetivo, método, resultado y postura del autor, distinguiendo una inferencia justificada de una exagerada.

vocabulario.es: datos declarados por los propios participantes

ensenanza.en: The opening of an abstract states its aim: what the authors set out to examine, and why the question matters.
ensenanza.es: El comienzo de un abstract enuncia su objetivo: lo que los autores se propusieron examinar y por qué importa la pregunta.
ensenanza.nota: Aim va seguido de to + verbo o de una oración con whether; se narra en pasado.

ensenanza.en: The method tells you who took part and for how long: we followed 240 adolescents in four schools for one year.
ensenanza.es: El método dice quién participó y durante cuánto tiempo: seguimos a 240 adolescentes en cuatro colegios durante un año.
ensenanza.nota: Fíjate en los números y en la duración: sirven para juzgar si el estudio es lo bastante grande.

ensenanza.en: Self-reported data, such as sleep diaries, are useful but open to error, because adolescents may remember their nights inaccurately.
ensenanza.es: Los datos declarados por los propios participantes, como los diarios de sueño, son útiles pero admiten errores, porque los adolescentes pueden recordar mal sus noches.
ensenanza.nota: Self-reported avisa de que la medición depende de lo que dicen los participantes, no de un instrumento.

ensenanza.en: These findings point to a benefit for adolescents, yet the authors avoid a causal link because the design cannot rule out other explanations.
ensenanza.es: Estos hallazgos apuntan a un beneficio para los adolescentes, pero los autores evitan un vínculo causal porque el diseño no puede descartar otras explicaciones.
ensenanza.nota: Point to es más cauto que prove; rule out significa descartar; una correlación no es una causa.

ensenanza.en: You may draw an inference only if it stays in line with the data; anything bolder needs further research.
ensenanza.es: Solo puedes sacar una inferencia si se mantiene en consonancia con los datos; algo más atrevido requiere más investigación.
ensenanza.nota: Una inferencia justificada no va más allá de lo que dicen los datos; further research señala el límite.

ensenanza.en: A hedged claim uses may, suggest or tend to, and this stance tells you how cautious the authors are about the benefit.
ensenanza.es: Una afirmación matizada usa may, suggest o tend to, y esta postura indica lo cautos que son los autores sobre el beneficio.
ensenanza.nota: Hedge significa atenuar una afirmación; los verbos modales y de cita revelan la postura.

explicacion.titulo: Leer un abstract: cuatro campos y una postura
explicacion.texto: Un abstract resume un estudio en un orden fijo: objetivo (aim: qué se quería averiguar), método (quién, cuántos, cuánto tiempo), resultados (qué se encontró, con cifras) y conclusión (qué significa y qué límites tiene). La postura del autor se lee en el lenguaje: suggest, may o point to indican cautela; show, prove o will indican seguridad. Antes de sacar una inferencia, comprueba que va en consonancia con los datos y que no confunde coincidencia con causa. Lee primero el objetivo y la última frase: ahí están la idea central y hasta dónde se atreve a llegar el autor.

formula.texto: The aim was to examine whether…
formula.nota: objetivo: la pregunta del estudio, con whether

formula.texto: We followed 240 adolescents for a year.
formula.nota: método: quién, cuántos y cuánto tiempo
resultados: lo que se midió, con cifras

formula.texto: These findings suggest that it may help.
formula.nota: conclusión y postura: suggest + may = cautela

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The authors prove that later start times help all teenagers.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The authors suggest that later start times may help some teenagers.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Un abstract no exagera: prove y all afirman más de lo que el estudio permite; suggest y may mantienen la cautela.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The aim of the study is examine whether sleep matters.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The aim of the study was to examine whether sleep matters.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Después de aim se usa to + verbo, y el abstract narra el estudio en pasado.

situacion.contexto: Sara y Carlos preparan una exposición y Carlos solo tiene dos minutos para entender un abstract.

dialogo.texto: I only have two minutes. How do I find out what this abstract really claims?
dialogo.traduccion: Solo tengo dos minutos. ¿Cómo averiguo qué afirma realmente este abstract?

dialogo.texto: Read the aim first, then the last sentence. The aim says they examined whether later starts help adolescents.
dialogo.traduccion: Lee primero el objetivo y después la última frase. El objetivo dice que examinaron si los comienzos más tardíos ayudan a los adolescentes.

dialogo.texto: And the last sentence says the findings point to a benefit, but they cannot rule out local factors.
dialogo.traduccion: Y la última frase dice que los hallazgos apuntan a un beneficio, pero no pueden descartar factores locales.

dialogo.texto: Exactly. That is a hedged claim, so you can draw an inference only in line with the data, not a causal link.
dialogo.traduccion: Exacto. Eso es una afirmación matizada, así que solo puedes sacar una inferencia en consonancia con los datos, no un vínculo causal.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué tipo de conclusión permite el abstract?

opciones.es: Una prudente, que no afirma que el horario cause el beneficio.
Una firme, que prueba que el horario tardío causa el beneficio.
Ninguna, porque los autores no pueden descartar factores locales.

item.feedback: Sara explica que es una afirmación matizada: se puede inferir un posible beneficio, pero no un vínculo causal.

guiada.consigna: ¿En qué campo del abstract aparece esta frase y qué información aporta?
guiada.texto: We followed 240 adolescents in four schools for one year; two schools moved the start of the day to nine o'clock, and two did not.
opciones: Method: it tells us who took part and how long the study lasted.
Aim: it tells us why the authors chose this question and what they hoped to find.
Conclusion: it tells us how far the authors are willing to go.
guiada.feedback: Es el método: dice cuántos estudiantes, en cuántos colegios y durante cuánto tiempo; no plantea la pregunta ni extrae conclusiones.
guiada.pista: Fíjate en las cifras y en la duración.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «El objetivo de este estudio era examinar si el ruido afecta a la memoria.»
guiada.texto: Researchers often open an abstract with a sentence of purpose. The ___ of this study was to examine whether background noise affects adolescents' memory.
guiada.feedback: Aim introduce la pregunta del estudio y va seguido de to + verbo.
guiada.pista: Sustantivo de tres letras que significa objetivo.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Estos hallazgos apuntan a un beneficio, pero hace falta más investigación.»
guiada.respuesta: These findings point to a benefit but further research is needed
guiada.feedback: Point to introduce el hallazgo con cautela y further research is needed marca el límite del estudio.
aceptadas: These findings point to a benefit, but further research is needed
guiada.pista: El sujeto These findings va primero; but separa las dos ideas.

practica.consigna: Lee el abstract y completa cuatro datos del estudio.
frases: Aim: to examine whether phone use in lessons ___ exam results.
Method: 600 students were tracked in ___ schools for two terms.
Result: schools with a ban scored about ___ per cent higher.
Stance: the authors say they cannot ___ out other explanations.
practica.feedback: Cada campo está en el abstract: la pregunta (lowers), la muestra (twelve schools), el resultado (four per cent) y el límite (rule out).
practica.texto: Aim: This study examined whether phone use in lessons lowers exam results among adolescents. Method: We tracked 600 students in twelve schools for two terms; half of the schools banned phones in class. Results: Students in schools with a ban scored about four per cent higher, but the difference narrowed in the second term. Conclusion: The findings point to a small benefit, although we cannot rule out other explanations, and further research is needed.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige cómo presentan los autores su resultado.
practica.audio: This study asked whether language apps help adults learn vocabulary. We tested two hundred adults for six weeks. Those who used the app remembered more words in a final test, but the difference was small, and most of the data were self-reported. We therefore describe the effect as small and call for further trials.
opciones: As a small improvement that they treat with care because of how it was measured.
As a small improvement that they see as important because it appeared in a final test.
As a small improvement that they put down to the fact that it lasted only six weeks.
practica.feedback: Los autores hablan de una diferencia pequeña y de datos declarados por los propios participantes, y piden más ensayos: prudencia, no entusiasmo.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué inferencia está justificada por estos resultados?
practica.texto: Results: Teenagers who slept nine hours scored five points higher on a memory test than those who slept six. Conclusion: Longer sleep may improve memory in adolescents, although all the participants were volunteers.
opciones: Longer sleep may help memory, although volunteers may not speak for all teenagers.
Anyone who sleeps nine hours instead of six will score higher on memory tests.
The five-point gain proves that longer sleep is what causes better memory.
practica.feedback: La conclusión usa may y reconoce que los participantes eran voluntarios; las otras dos frases generalizan o afirman una causa sin apoyo en los datos.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué inferencia va más allá de lo que sostiene el abstract?
evaluacion.texto: Aim: This study examined whether later school start times improve the sleep and attention of adolescents. Method: We followed 240 students in four schools for one year; two schools moved the start of the day to nine o'clock, and two did not. Results: At the later schools, students slept about fifty minutes longer each night and reported better attention, although attention was self-reported. Conclusion: These findings point to a possible benefit. Because all four schools were in one city, we cannot rule out local factors, and further research is needed.
opciones: Every school in every country will see better attention if lessons start later.
Later starts may help adolescents sleep longer, at least in this city.
The attention results rest partly on what students said about themselves.
The study cannot show that the later start, rather than local factors, caused the gains.
evaluacion.feedback: El abstract solo apunta a un posible beneficio en cuatro colegios de una ciudad; extenderlo a todos los colegios del mundo es una exageración.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige la postura de los autores ante su propia hipótesis.
evaluacion.audio: Our sample was small, sixty runners, and all of them were club members. Those who slept longer reported fewer injuries. We do not claim that sleep prevents injury. The data are in line with that idea, nothing more, and any stronger statement would need further trials with a wider group of athletes.
opciones: Cautious: the data fit the idea, but they do not claim it is proven.
Confident: the data prove the idea, but they ask for further trials anyway.
Sceptical: they reject the idea because the sample was made up of club members.
evaluacion.feedback: Dicen que los datos están «in line with» la idea, «nothing more»: postura prudente, ni de prueba ni de rechazo.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Los datos están en consonancia con estudios anteriores.»
evaluacion.texto: The authors write that the sleep data are in ___ with earlier studies, which reported the same pattern in younger children.
evaluacion.feedback: In line with significa «en consonancia con»; in keeping with e in agreement with son variantes posibles.

evaluacion.consigna: Resume el abstract: objetivo, resultado y postura de los autores.
evaluacion.texto: Aim: This study examined whether later school start times improve the sleep and attention of adolescents. Method: We followed 240 students in four schools for one year; two schools moved the start of the day to nine o'clock, and two did not. Results: At the later schools, students slept about fifty minutes longer each night and reported better attention, although attention was self-reported. Conclusion: These findings point to a possible benefit. Because all four schools were in one city, we cannot rule out local factors, and further research is needed.
evaluacion.respuesta: The study examined whether later school start times improve the sleep and attention of adolescents. Students at the later schools slept about fifty minutes longer, and the authors say the findings point to a possible benefit, but they cannot rule out local factors.
aceptadas: The aim was to examine whether starting school later improves sleep and attention. Students at the later schools slept fifty minutes longer, which may suggest a benefit, although further research is needed because local factors cannot be ruled out.

This study asked whether later starts help teenagers. The students who started later slept longer, and the authors say it could help, but they cannot say for sure because all four schools were in one city.
evaluacion.feedback: Un buen resumen recoge la pregunta, el dato principal y la prudencia de los autores sin exagerarla.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué advierte el autor sobre los colegios que aceptan cambiar su horario?
repaso.texto: Discussion: Although students at the later schools slept longer, the design cannot show that the timetable caused the change. It is possible that schools which agree to change their timetables are already more supportive of students' wellbeing. Until that possibility is tested, the authors advise readers to treat the result as a first step rather than an answer.
opciones: That the schools studied may differ from others in ways that matter for the result.
That the schools that refused to change their timetables were unfairly treated.
That supportive schools always produce students who sleep longer than students in other schools do.
That the later timetable is useless in every school that accepts it.
repaso.feedback: El autor sugiere que los colegios que aceptan el cambio ya pueden ser distintos (más comprensivos), y eso podría explicar el resultado.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Los autores son cautos porque no pueden descartar otras explicaciones.»
repaso.respuesta: The authors are cautious because they cannot rule out other explanations
repaso.feedback: Rule out other explanations es la fórmula para descartar alternativas, y because introduce la razón de la cautela.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Halló que ambas cosas coinciden, pero no puede probar un vínculo causal.»
repaso.texto: The study found that two things tend to happen together. However, the design cannot show a ___ link between them, because it did not control other factors.
repaso.feedback: A causal link es un vínculo de causa y efecto; aquí el autor señala que coincidir no equivale a causar.

classes.objetivo: Parafrasear un párrafo atribuyendo las ideas con verbos de cita adecuados (argue, claim, maintain, acknowledge, according to) y condensándolo con una nominalización.

ensenanza.en: To paraphrase a source, change the structure as well as the words, and keep the original meaning intact.
ensenanza.es: Para parafrasear una fuente, cambia la estructura además de las palabras y conserva intacto el significado original.
ensenanza.nota: Cambiar dos o tres palabras no es parafrasear: hay que reorganizar la frase.

ensenanza.en: Copying a sentence verbatim and changing two words is not paraphrasing; it is copying with a small disguise.
ensenanza.es: Copiar una frase textualmente y cambiar dos palabras no es parafrasear; es copiar con un pequeño disfraz.
ensenanza.nota: Verbatim significa «palabra por palabra»; si copias así, debes citar con comillas.

ensenanza.en: According to the survey, cycling has doubled: a reporting verb shows how far you agree with the source.
ensenanza.es: Según la encuesta, el ciclismo se ha duplicado: un verbo de cita muestra hasta qué punto estás de acuerdo con la fuente.
ensenanza.nota: According to (con to) introduce una fuente neutral; el verbo de cita añade tu actitud.

ensenanza.en: Use claim to distance yourself from a statement that you doubt, and argue when you find the reasons persuasive.
ensenanza.es: Usa claim para distanciarte de una afirmación de la que dudas, y argue cuando las razones te parezcan convincentes.
ensenanza.nota: Claim toma distancia; argue presenta una tesis defendida con razones.

ensenanza.en: Planners maintain that safer streets attract customers, and some economists contend that the investment pays for itself.
ensenanza.es: Los urbanistas sostienen que las calles más seguras atraen clientes, y algunos economistas afirman que la inversión se paga sola.
ensenanza.nota: Maintain indica firmeza; contend es más formal, propio de textos académicos.

ensenanza.en: A careful writer will point out a weakness, acknowledge a limit or take issue with a doubtful claim, without attributing anything twice.
ensenanza.es: Un autor cuidadoso señalará una debilidad, reconocerá un límite o discrepará de una afirmación dudosa, sin atribuir nada dos veces.
ensenanza.nota: Cada verbo de cita expresa una función: señalar, admitir o discrepar; una sola atribución por idea.

explicacion.titulo: Parafrasear y atribuir: los verbos de cita
explicacion.texto: Parafrasear es contar la idea de otra persona con tu propia estructura y tus palabras, y atribuirla siempre. El verbo de cita muestra cómo te sitúas: according to (con to) introduce una fuente neutral; argue, maintain y contend presentan una tesis defendida; claim toma distancia; acknowledge admite un límite; point out hace notar un dato. Tras el verbo va that + oración. Para condensar, usa nominalizaciones («cycling grew» pasa a «the growth in cycling») y no atribuyas dos veces: According to… y argue juntos sobran. Copiar textualmente sin comillas no es parafrasear.

patron.texto: Fuente + verbo de cita + that + idea condensada:

formula.nota: fuente: quién lo dice (o bien According to the report, sin verbo de cita)

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: According to the authors, they argue that the plan works.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The authors argue that the plan works.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Según los autores y «ellos sostienen» repiten la atribución; basta con una de las dos.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: According the report, bicycle use has doubled.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: According to the report, bicycle use has doubled.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En inglés es according to; en español «según» no lleva preposición y por eso se olvida el to.

situacion.contexto: Mia y Tom preparan un ensayo y Mia tiene que parafrasear un párrafo sin copiar su estructura.

dialogo.texto: I have to paraphrase this paragraph, and I have copied half of it verbatim without noticing.
dialogo.traduccion: Tengo que parafrasear este párrafo y he copiado la mitad textualmente sin darme cuenta.

dialogo.texto: Change the structure, not only the words. And say who said it: according to the report, or the authors argue that.
dialogo.traduccion: Cambia la estructura, no solo las palabras. Y di quién lo dijo: según el informe, o los autores sostienen que.

dialogo.texto: What about the critics? I think their figures are weak, but I do not want to sound rude.
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Y los críticos? Creo que sus cifras son débiles, pero no quiero sonar descortés.

dialogo.texto: Write that they claim the figures are final. That is polite, and it lets you distance yourself from the statement.
dialogo.traduccion: Escribe que afirman que las cifras son definitivas. Es cortés y te permite distanciarte de esa afirmación.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿por qué aconseja Tom usar claim al hablar de los críticos?

opciones.es: Porque permite distanciarse de la afirmación sin resultar descortés.
Porque indica que tú compartes la opinión de los críticos.
Porque es el verbo más formal para citar cualquier fuente académica.

item.feedback: Tom dice que claim es cortés y que permite distanciarse de la afirmación de los críticos.

guiada.consigna: Quieres dejar claro que dudas de lo que afirma la fuente. ¿Qué frase eliges?
guiada.texto: Source: An online post says that the new lanes were cheap to build, yet the council's own accounts show costs twice as high as planned.
opciones: Some commentators claim that the lanes were cheap, yet the council's accounts suggest otherwise.
Some commentators acknowledge that the lanes were cheap, yet the council's accounts suggest otherwise.
Some commentators maintain that the lanes were cheap, yet the council's accounts suggest otherwise.
guiada.feedback: Claim toma distancia de lo dicho; acknowledge admite que es verdad y maintain sugiere una convicción firme que tú no compartes.
guiada.pista: Busca el verbo que toma distancia de la afirmación.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Según el segundo informe, el tráfico del centro ha bajado un nueve por ciento.»
guiada.texto: Two reports were published last week. ___ to the second, traffic in the centre has fallen by nine per cent.
guiada.feedback: Según se dice According to; sin to la atribución es incorrecta.
guiada.pista: Se escribe con mayúscula al empezar la frase.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Los autores reconocen que su muestra era demasiado pequeña.»
guiada.respuesta: The authors acknowledge that their sample was too small
guiada.feedback: Acknowledge introduce un límite que los propios autores admiten, seguido de that + oración.
guiada.pista: El sujeto The authors va primero; that abre la oración subordinada.

practica.consigna: Elige la paráfrasis que cambia la estructura y mantiene el sentido.
practica.texto: Original (from a city report): Many more people started cycling after the city built new lanes, and this helped to cut traffic in the centre.
opciones: According to the report, the new lanes led to a growth in cycling and a reduction in traffic in the centre.
Many more people began cycling after the city made new lanes, and this helped to cut down traffic in the centre of town.
According to the report, the growth in cycling led to the construction of the new lanes in the city.
practica.feedback: Se atribuye la idea con According to y se nominaliza (growth, reduction); otra opción solo cambia palabras sueltas y otra invierte la causa.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué actitud muestra la hablante hacia lo que dicen los críticos.
practica.audio: The critics claim that the lanes hurt local shops. The shop owners I spoke to say otherwise, and the figures, which are still partial, seem to support them. I would therefore treat that claim with care until someone publishes the full sales data.
opciones: She doubts it and keeps her distance until fuller evidence is published.
She rejects it outright, since the shop owners have proved it wrong.
She accepts it as probable, although she would like more figures.
practica.feedback: El verbo claim y la frase «treat that claim with care» muestran que la hablante duda y se distancia hasta ver los datos completos.

practica.consigna: Completa: «La investigadora señala que las ventas junto a los carriles han subido.»
practica.texto: The researcher ___ out that shops along the lanes have seen their sales grow, although she admits that her sample is small.
practica.feedback: Point out significa «hacer notar»; con she en presente necesita -s.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué implica el uso de «claim» en este párrafo?
evaluacion.texto: Some commentators claim that the plan will pay for itself within five years. They may be right, but they do not say how they reached that figure, and the council's own accounts point the other way. Until someone explains the figure, I shall treat the claim as a hope rather than a forecast.
opciones: That the writer doubts the statement and will not accept it without evidence.
That the writer accepts the figure but wants the council to publish it.
That the commentators are unreliable people whose opinions should be ignored entirely.
That the writer believes the council's accounts are false and were written to give readers a false picture.
evaluacion.feedback: Claim toma distancia, y el final («a hope rather than a forecast») confirma que el autor no acepta la cifra sin pruebas.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige cómo matiza el planificador el dato de la investigadora.
evaluacion.audio: The report notes that cycling has grown by two hundred per cent in five years. The lead author stresses that the growth is concentrated in the city centre, and she concedes that data from the areas outside the centre are very limited. A planner quoted in the same report takes issue with that figure: he says that the starting number was very low, so a large percentage does not mean a large number of people.
opciones: It looks bigger than it is, because it started from a very low base.
It was measured wrongly, because the data from outside the centre are limited.
It is only true of the city centre, where the authors collected their figures.
evaluacion.feedback: El planificador discrepa de esa cifra porque partía de una cifra muy baja; las otras opciones atribuyen al planificador lo que dice la autora principal.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Los autores reconocen que su encuesta fue limitada y piden una mayor.»
evaluacion.texto: The authors ___ that their survey was limited, and they ask the council to repeat it next year with a larger sample.
evaluacion.feedback: Acknowledge introduce una limitación admitida por los propios autores.

evaluacion.consigna: Parafrasea el informe en 100–140 palabras: dos verbos de cita y una nominalización.
evaluacion.texto: Five years ago, the city council decided to build more than one hundred kilometres of protected bike lanes. At first, many residents opposed the plan, and shop owners were especially worried, because they assumed that fewer parking places would mean fewer customers. However, the figures published this spring tell a different story. The proportion of people who cycle to work has risen from three per cent to eleven per cent, while car traffic in the centre has fallen by nine per cent. Air quality has improved, the main streets are quieter, and several schools report that more pupils now arrive by bicycle. The researcher who led the study argues that the investment has already paid for itself, because the city now spends less on road repairs and on health care. She points out that sales in the shops along the new lanes have grown by six per cent. Nevertheless, some critics claim that the results for small shops are unreliable, since only forty businesses answered the survey. The researcher acknowledges this limitation, and she suggests that the council should repeat the survey next year with a larger sample. Meanwhile, the council hopes to build more lanes in the north of the city, although it has not yet said who will pay for them.
evaluacion.respuesta: According to the council's study, the building of more than a hundred kilometres of new lanes for cyclists has been followed by a sharp growth in commuter cycling, from 3 to 11 per cent, and by a reduction in central traffic of nine per cent. Early opposition, especially from shopkeepers who feared losing customers to reduced parking, has proved wrong. The lead researcher argues that the scheme has already earned back its cost, since spending on road maintenance and health care has dropped, and she notes that shops beside the lanes now earn six per cent more. Some critics claim, however, that the findings for small firms cannot be trusted, because just forty of them replied. The researcher concedes that this is a weakness and recommends a second, larger survey next year, while the council, for its part, is considering further routes outside the centre but has not explained where the money will come from.
aceptadas: Since the council built its protected bike lanes, the published figures point to a rise in cycling to work and a fall in traffic, together with cleaner air. The lead researcher maintains that the project has already repaid its cost, noting lower spending on roads and health care and higher sales in shops beside the lanes. Some critics claim that the evidence on small businesses is unreliable, since few of them replied. She acknowledges that weakness and recommends a second, larger survey next year, while the council is already looking at further routes for cyclists.

Five years on, the study reports a growth in cycling and a decrease in central traffic, together with cleaner air and quieter streets. The lead researcher contends that the project has paid back its cost, because road repairs and health care now cost less, and she adds that shops beside the lanes are selling more. Critics claim that the findings on small shops cannot be trusted, since only forty of them replied. She admits this limit and suggests repeating the survey after a year with a wider sample, while the council is looking at further routes outside the centre.
evaluacion.feedback: Una buena paráfrasis cambia la estructura, atribuye cada idea una sola vez con verbos distintos, condensa con nominalizaciones y no copia frases del original.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué sugiere el autor sobre las preguntas de la encuesta que no se publican?
repaso.texto: The council argues that the lanes are a success, but its figures come from its own survey, and it has not published the questions. Nobody outside the council can tell whether residents were asked fairly. It may be a good survey; it may not. Until the council shows its method, the claim rests on trust.
opciones: That the results cannot be checked, so the council's argument deserves care.
That the council has lied on purpose about the survey results.
That the survey questions were too difficult for residents to answer.
That the survey is the only evidence that the council could have used.
repaso.feedback: Sin las preguntas no se puede verificar la encuesta: el autor invita a la cautela, pero no acusa al municipio de mentir.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «La investigadora señala un fallo pero mantiene su opinión.»
repaso.respuesta: The researcher points out a flaw but maintains her view
repaso.feedback: Points out señala el fallo y maintains her view mantiene la tesis; but une ambas ideas.

repaso.consigna: Relaciona cada expresión de cita con su función en el texto.
repaso.feedback: Cada verbo cumple una función distinta: distanciarse, defender, admitir y discrepar.

classes.objetivo: Resumir un estudio sencillo ante el grupo con registro académico: objetivo, método, resultado, una pasiva impersonal y una respuesta prudente a una duda.

ensenanza.en: Briefly, the aim was to compare two groups of adults over eight weeks; it is worth noting that all were volunteers.
ensenanza.es: Brevemente, el objetivo era comparar dos grupos de adultos durante ocho semanas; conviene señalar que todos eran voluntarios.
ensenanza.nota: Briefly abre un resumen condensado; it is worth noting introduce un dato que matiza lo anterior.

ensenanza.en: It is widely assumed that exercise sharpens memory, although that idea has rarely been tested in a controlled trial.
ensenanza.es: Se da por supuesto que el ejercicio agudiza la memoria, aunque esa idea rara vez se ha puesto a prueba en un ensayo controlado.
ensenanza.nota: La pasiva impersonal presenta una opinión general sin decir quién la sostiene; it es obligatorio en inglés.

ensenanza.en: It has been shown that daily walkers scored higher, yet part of the difference can be attributed to motivation.
ensenanza.es: Se ha demostrado que quienes caminan a diario obtuvieron mejores puntuaciones, pero parte de la diferencia puede atribuirse a la motivación.
ensenanza.nota: It has been shown = resultado establecido; be attributed to introduce una explicación posible.

ensenanza.en: The effect is thought to be small, and a pilot study of forty adults cannot account for every variable.
ensenanza.es: Se piensa que el efecto es pequeño, y un estudio piloto con cuarenta adultos no puede explicar todas las variables.
ensenanza.nota: Variante personal de la impersonal: sujeto + be + participio + to + verbo; account for = explicar.

ensenanza.en: Overall, the benefit is small, and it is difficult to generalise from one group of volunteers to everyone.
ensenanza.es: En conjunto, el beneficio es pequeño, y es difícil generalizar a partir de un grupo de voluntarios a todo el mundo.
ensenanza.nota: Overall condensa el resultado; it is difficult to generalise es la respuesta prudente ante quien pregunta si vale para todos.

ensenanza.en: On balance, the conclusion is tentative; it is thought to hold for adults, with the proviso that no teenagers were tested.
ensenanza.es: Sopesándolo todo, la conclusión es provisional; se piensa que vale para adultos, con la salvedad de que no se probó con adolescentes.
ensenanza.nota: On balance cierra el resumen con un juicio global; with the proviso that añade la condición que limita la conclusión.

explicacion.titulo: Resumir un estudio: pasiva impersonal y cautela
explicacion.texto: Al resumir un estudio para tu grupo, sigue el orden objetivo, método, resultado y límite. Briefly y overall ayudan a condensar, y on balance cierra con un juicio global. Para presentar ideas sin decir quién las sostiene, usa la pasiva impersonal: It is assumed / believed / thought that… o It has been shown that…, con el sujeto it obligatorio (en español basta «se piensa que»). Cuando alguien pregunte si el resultado vale para todos, responde con prudencia: It is difficult to generalise… y una conclusión provisional, con la salvedad que corresponda.

formula.nota: it + be + participio: opinión general sin decir quién

formula.texto: The effect is thought to be small.
formula.nota: variante personal: sujeto + be + participio + to + verbo

filas.texto: The effect is thought to be small.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: It has shown that later start times improve attention.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: It has been shown that later start times improve attention.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En la pasiva impersonal falta been: es has been + participio, no has + participio.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Is thought that the effect is small.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: It is thought that the effect is small.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En inglés la oración necesita sujeto: aunque en español se dice «se piensa que», aquí hay que escribir it.

situacion.contexto: Sara presenta un estudio al grupo de estudio y Carlos le hace una pregunta difícil sobre lo que encontraron.

dialogo.texto: Briefly, the aim was to compare two groups of adults over eight weeks, and overall the group that walked concentrated better.
dialogo.traduccion: Brevemente, el objetivo era comparar dos grupos de adultos durante ocho semanas y, en conjunto, el grupo que caminó se concentró mejor.

dialogo.texto: So can we say that walking improves concentration for everyone?
dialogo.traduccion: Entonces, ¿podemos decir que caminar mejora la concentración de todos?

dialogo.texto: Not quite. It is worth noting that all the adults were volunteers, so it is difficult to generalise the result.
dialogo.traduccion: No exactamente. Conviene señalar que todos los adultos eran voluntarios, así que es difícil generalizar el resultado.

dialogo.texto: I see. On balance, then, the conclusion is tentative, with the proviso that nobody older was tested.
dialogo.traduccion: Ya veo. Entonces, sopesándolo todo, la conclusión es provisional, con la salvedad de que nadie mayor participó.

dialogo.texto: Exactly, and that is how I will put it in my summary.
dialogo.traduccion: Exacto, y así lo diré en mi resumen.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué responde Sara cuando Carlos pregunta si vale para todos?

opciones.es: Que es difícil generalizar porque todos los participantes eran voluntarios.
Que sí vale para todos, porque el grupo que caminó se concentró mejor.
Que no puede responder porque el estudio duró solo ocho semanas.

item.feedback: Sara contesta con cautela: «it is difficult to generalise the result» porque los participantes eran todos voluntarios.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Se ha demostrado que dormir bien ayuda a la memoria.»
guiada.texto: Researchers do not always name who holds an idea. They write instead: It has been ___ that regular sleep improves memory, although the effect is small.
guiada.feedback: La pasiva impersonal es It has been + participio + that; shown presenta un resultado ya establecido.
guiada.pista: Participio de show: It has been ___ that…

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué frase es una pasiva impersonal bien formada y cautelosa?
guiada.texto: You want to report a finding without saying who holds the view, and you want to sound cautious about how far it applies.
opciones: It is thought that the effect is small and may not apply to older adults.
Is thought that the effect is small and may not apply to older adults.
It thinks that the effect is small and may not apply to older adults.
guiada.feedback: La estructura correcta necesita it como sujeto y be + participio: It is thought that…; las otras dos omiten el sujeto o usan un verbo activo.
guiada.pista: En inglés el sujeto it es obligatorio; el verbo va en pasiva.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Brevemente, el objetivo era comparar dos grupos de adultos.»
guiada.respuesta: Briefly, the aim was to compare two groups of adults
guiada.feedback: Briefly abre el resumen; the aim was to + verbo enuncia el objetivo en pasado.
aceptadas: Briefly the aim was to compare two groups of adults
guiada.pista: Briefly va al principio, seguido de una coma.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué concluye el hablante.
practica.audio: Overall, the study suggests a small benefit, but the sample came from only one class, so it is difficult to generalise. It is thought that the effect would be stronger with older students, although nobody has tested that yet.
opciones: The benefit is small, and nobody knows yet whether it applies elsewhere or grows with age.
The benefit is small, though it is certain to apply to other classes and age groups.
The benefit is small, and the study shows that it would be stronger with older students.
practica.feedback: El hablante dice que el beneficio es pequeño y difícil de generalizar, y que un efecto mayor con estudiantes mayores es solo una suposición («nobody has tested that yet»).

practica.consigna: Un compañero pregunta si el resultado vale para todos. ¿Qué respuesta es la más prudente?
practica.texto: A classmate asks whether the walking results apply to everyone. The study involved forty adults, all of them volunteers, and all under thirty.
opciones: It is difficult to generalise, since the participants were few, young and volunteers.
It has been shown that the result holds for everyone, since they were volunteers.
It is widely assumed that volunteers think like everybody else, so the answer is yes.
practica.feedback: La respuesta prudente reconoce el límite de la muestra con it is difficult to generalise; las otras dos extienden el resultado sin pruebas.

practica.consigna: Completa: «En conjunto, los resultados son alentadores.»
practica.texto: The study lasted only eight weeks and involved a single group. ___, the results are encouraging, but they should be treated as a first step.
practica.feedback: Overall condensa el balance del estudio al comienzo de la frase.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué postura transmite la autora de este resumen?
evaluacion.texto: Briefly, the study compared two groups of adults over eight weeks. Overall, those who walked thirty minutes a day scored eight per cent higher on a memory test. It has been shown that exercise helps the mind, so everyone should start walking today. The study itself used only volunteers, but that detail did not seem worth a mention.
opciones: Confident to the point of overstating what the study can actually show.
Balanced: she weighs the result against its limits before she reaches a conclusion.
Critical of the study, which she thinks is too small to tell us anything.
Neutral, simply repeating the authors' claims without any opinion of her own.
evaluacion.feedback: Dice «everyone should start walking today» a partir de una muestra de voluntarios y descarta ese límite como un detalle sin importancia: su seguridad va más allá de lo que el estudio permite.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige cómo responde el ponente a la pregunta del público.
evaluacion.audio: Someone asked me whether exercise improves memory for everyone. Not quite. The study followed sixty adults, all of them volunteers, and the improvement was about eight per cent. It is thought that exercise helps, and the findings are in line with earlier work, but it is difficult to generalise from volunteers. On balance, the conclusion is tentative, with the proviso that older adults were not tested. I should add that this was a pilot study with a small sample, so it is thought that a larger trial would give a clearer picture, but nobody can say for certain until it is carried out.
opciones: Not yet: the result is promising but cannot safely be extended to everyone.
Yes, in general: the findings match earlier work, so the result can be extended.
No: the pilot study was too small to show anything at all about exercise.
evaluacion.feedback: El ponente dice «Not quite»: el resultado es prometedor y coincide con trabajos previos, pero con voluntarios es difícil generalizar y faltan los mayores; tampoco descarta el efecto.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Parte de la mejora puede atribuirse a que todos eran voluntarios entusiastas.»
evaluacion.texto: The improvement is thought to be small, and part of it may be ___ to the fact that all the participants were eager volunteers.
evaluacion.feedback: Be attributed to significa «atribuirse a»; due to y ascribed to son variantes cercanas.

evaluacion.consigna: Resume el estudio: objetivo, método, resultado, pasiva impersonal y respuesta.
evaluacion.texto: Estudio: ¿tomar apuntes a mano ayuda a recordar más que escribirlos en el teclado? 120 estudiantes durante tres semanas; la mitad escribió a mano. Los que escribieron a mano recordaron un 6 % más en una prueba final. Todos venían de un mismo colegio. Un compañero pregunta: «¿Podemos decir que escribir a mano es mejor para la memoria?» Escribe el resumen, usa una pasiva impersonal y responde con cautela.
evaluacion.respuesta: The aim of this study was to examine whether taking notes by hand helps students remember more than typing. Briefly, one hundred and twenty students were followed for three weeks, and half of them wrote their notes by hand. Overall, the students who wrote by hand recalled six per cent more in a final test. It is widely assumed that handwriting is better for memory, and these findings are in line with that idea. It is worth noting that part of the difference may be attributed to motivation, since those students were all volunteers. To answer your question, we cannot say that handwriting is better for everyone, because all the participants came from one college, and it is difficult to generalise from a single group. On balance, the conclusion is tentative, and further research with students of different ages is needed before anyone gives firm advice to students.
aceptadas: This study asked whether taking notes by hand is better for memory than typing them. Briefly, a hundred and twenty students took part for three weeks, and half of them wrote by hand. Overall, the handwriters remembered six per cent more in the final test. It is often believed that writing by hand helps memory, and the results are in line with that view. However, everybody came from the same college, so we cannot say that handwriting is better for all students; it is difficult to generalise from one school. It is worth noting that some of the difference could be attributed to motivation. The conclusion is tentative, and further research is needed.

The aim was to examine whether students who write their notes by hand remember more than students who type. Briefly, one hundred and twenty students were tested over three weeks, and half of them used pens. Overall, the handwriters recalled six per cent more. It is thought that handwriting slows people down and helps them think, which is in line with these findings. To answer your question, it is difficult to generalise, since every participant belonged to one college, and we cannot say that the method works for everyone. On balance, the conclusion is tentative, with the proviso that more research is needed with different groups of students.
evaluacion.feedback: Un resumen completo recorre objetivo, método, resultado y límite, usa una pasiva impersonal y responde a la duda con prudencia.

repaso.consigna: ¿Con qué propósito escribe la autora «I would not generalise beyond first-year students»?
repaso.texto: Dear group, here is the summary you asked for. The aim was to compare two methods of revision. It has been shown that testing yourself beats reading your notes again, but the effect is thought to be smaller for difficult topics. I would not generalise from first-year students to students in later years. I hope that answers your question, and I am happy to share the paper.
opciones: To limit her answer to the kind of students that the study actually examined.
To say that first-year students are the only ones who should revise in this way.
To refuse to answer her classmate's question about the paper.
To warn that the paper is unreliable because it is old.
repaso.feedback: Delimita su respuesta a los estudiantes del estudio: es la prudencia de quien no extiende el resultado más allá de la muestra.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Se cree ampliamente que el efecto es pequeño.»
repaso.respuesta: It is widely believed that the effect is small
repaso.feedback: It is widely believed that + oración es la pasiva impersonal con un adverbio de grado; it es obligatorio.

repaso.consigna: Relaciona cada fórmula del resumen con su sentido.
pares: The difference can be attributed to…
repaso.feedback: Cada fórmula cumple una función: dar un resultado establecido, añadir un matiz, explicar una diferencia y cerrar con un balance.

notes: C31-C35 revisados contra el mapa n10 (concepto, fase, canDo, tarea) y el contrato C1; sin P0/P1 pendientes.
C31: distractor 'Approving' del escuchar e1 sustituido por un cercano (rechazo total); e2 ya no repite la frase de enseñanza de lend itself to; rúbrica de e3 sin verbos sueltos.
C32: p0 desambiguado (robust vs compelling por pistas léxicas); traducción de p2 corregida ('realizó una sola vez'); opciones de situación y g1 pasan a casi-aciertos.
C33: aceptadas de p0/e2/r2 depuradas (sin formas agramaticales); p2 y situación con distractores de sobregeneralización; rúbrica e3 sin 'a benefit' suelto.

C34: fuente reescrita a 213 palabras y modelo de 155 sin frases copiadas (builder exige >=133); consigna/rúbrica/aceptadas coherentes (100-140 palabras, rango 95-170); patrón ya no duplica atribución; grupos de evidencia por función (verbo de cita / crítica o reconocimiento / nominalización / tema) con variantes s/ed, no exigen un verbo concreto.
C35: e0 ya no es autocontradictorio; e1 con monólogo coherente (sesenta adultos) y distractores cercanos; p0 sin opción claramente más larga.
P2 abiertos: C33 e0 y e3 comparten el mismo abstract; las tareas largas del mapa (60-80 palabras de paráfrasis, 8 ítems) se adaptan al formato compacto y al 70 % que exige el constructor.
